condition: Euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis after surgery (SGLT2 inhibitor not withheld)
summary: 61-year-old woman on empagliflozin, day 2 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy with poor oral intake: vomiting, abdominal pain, tachypnoea; glucose 9.8 mmol/L, pH 7.18, bicarbonate 10, ketones 5.4 mmol/L.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Vomiting and breathlessness two days after gallbladder operation
inputs.hpi: Day 2 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Empagliflozin and metformin were taken until the morning of surgery and restarted yesterday. Nauseated since surgery, eating very little; vomited four times today. Vague generalised abdominal ache, feels breathless and weak. Glucose readings 8–10 mmol/L so no insulin given.

exam.general: Dry mucous membranes. Deep sighing respiration. HR 112, BP 108/68, RR 28, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.9°C.
exam.abdomen: Port sites clean. Soft, mild generalised tenderness, no peritonism.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis (SGLT2 inhibitor) — day 2 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Euglycaemic DKA: glucose 9.8 mmol/L, pH 7.18, bicarbonate 10, ketones 5.4 mmol/L, on empagliflozin continued peri-operatively. Stop empagliflozin; DKA protocol with fixed-rate insulin and glucose.

mustNotMiss.note: Euglycaemic DKA: the glucose is normal, so a glucose-driven rule will not find it.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: acute cholecystitis (the gallbladder was removed 2 days ago), post-operative ileus, bowel obstruction. PANE has no DKA node, and no rule reads the ketone, pH or bicarbonate results.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add a hard safety rule: ketones ≥3 mmol/L or pH <7.3/bicarbonate <15 → DKA alarm regardless of glucose, with an SGLT2i-specific 'euglycaemic DKA' message; add metabolic mimics to PANE or a separate 'non-surgical causes' list.

mustNotMiss.note: Day 2 after cholecystectomy with abdominal pain: bile leak remains in the differential.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: No post-cholecystectomy complication node (bile leak) in PANE; cholecystitis ranks first after cholecystectomy because nothing reads the surgical history.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: suppress gallbladder diagnoses after cholecystectomy; add bile leak / post-operative collection nodes.

mustInclude.note: Fixed-rate IV insulin with 10% glucose alongside because the glucose is not high.

mustExclude.note: No generalised peritonitis or perforation: an emergency-laparotomy consent line is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: JBDS — management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults
guideline.section: DKA: ketonaemia ≥3.0 mmol/L (or ketonuria ≥2+), bicarbonate <15 mmol/L and/or pH <7.3; euglycaemic DKA in people on SGLT2 inhibitors (glucose may be normal); stop the SGLT2 inhibitor; fixed-rate IV insulin infusion with glucose 10% when glucose is below 14 mmol/L
guideline.citation: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care. The management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults. 2023 update.

guideline.name: CPOC guideline — perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery
guideline.section: SGLT2 inhibitors: omit the day before and the day of surgery, check ketones; sulfonylureas omitted on the day of surgery; people with diabetes early on the list; capillary glucose monitoring; VRIII when more than one meal will be missed or in emergency surgery; type 1 diabetes: never omit basal insulin (continue long-acting insulin, usually at a reduced dose) alongside VRIII
guideline.citation: Centre for Perioperative Care. Guideline for perioperative care for people with diabetes mellitus undergoing elective and emergency surgery. London: CPOC; 2021 (updated 2022).

rationale: Permutation: the complication the base case prevents. A dangerous mimic of post-operative ileus/leak; glucose is not raised, so glucose-threshold rules do not fire. Tests the DKA diagnosis, alarm, ketone/gas tests and stopping the SGLT2 inhibitor.
